transcript.text: theres a funny smell from my oven when its on

A funny smell when you first turn on an oven is quite common. In many cases, especially with new ovens or if they haven't been used for a while, it's just the 'burning off' of factory protective oils or accumulated dust from the heating elements. This usually goes away after running the oven empty at a high temperature (around 200°C) for about 30–60 minutes. However, we need to rule out something more serious. Could you tell me: is the smell more like plastic/metal burning (which suggests an electrical fault), or does it smell like dust/smoke/burnt food? Also, please check behind and around the oven carefully. Is there any visible charring, melting, or discoloration on the mains cable where it connects to the back of the appliance? If you see any damage there, stop using it immediately and switch off the power at the wall.
more like hot plastic or electrical I think, and it seems to come from behind or underneath, not inside the oven. I can't pull the cooker out to look at the cable, it's too heavy and I'm on my own

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. This points to a serious electrical fault—most likely a loose or overheating connection where the main power cable enters the back of the cooker (the terminal block). This can melt insulation and create a fire hazard. Since you cannot move the heavy cooker to inspect it yourself, please do not try to force it. You must stop using the oven immediately. Switch off the power at the wall isolator or consumer unit (fuse box) until a qualified engineer can safely disconnect the appliance, inspect the terminal block and wiring, and carry out any necessary repairs. Do not attempt to use the oven again until this has been checked.

candidates: Normal 'burning off' of factory residues or protective oils (high)
Food spillage or grease burning on the oven floor or heating element (medium)
plan: The fault they reported is: "funny smell when it's on". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the safe checks that best tell those causes apart (most useful and simplest first, usually two to four), each with why it helps and what each result would mean; or, if one question would settle it sooner, ask that. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.
